'''''Pteronisculus''''' is an [[extinct]] [[genus]] of prehistoric [[ray-finned fish]] that lived during the [[Early Triassic]] and [[Middle Triassic]] [[epoch (geology)|epochs]] of the [[Triassic]] [[period (geology)|period]] worldwide.<ref name="doi.org"/> 

It was first described under the name "'''''Glaucolepis'''''" by [[Erik Stensiö]] in 1921 and was later shown to be a [[synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] of ''Pteronisculus'' described by [[Errol White]] in 1933. However, because the name "''Glaucolepis''" is preoccupied (it had already been given to the extant [[lepidopteran]] insect ''[[Glaucolepis]]'' Braun, 1917), ''Pteronisculus'' became the valid genus name for the Triassic fish.<ref name="White1940">{{cite journal |last1=White |first1=Errol I. |last2=Moy-Thomas |first2=James A. |date=1940 |title=VII.—Notes on the nomenclature of fossil fishes. Part II. Homonyms D–L |journal= Annals and Magazine of Natural History |series=11 |volume=6 |issue=31 |pages=98–103 |doi=10.1080/03745481.1940.9723659}}</ref>

==Appearance and distribution==
Like many other early ray-finned fishes, ''Pteronisculus'' had a bullet-shaped skull with large eyes near the front end, and a large [[gape]] armed with small to large, conical teeth. Its body was covered with small rhombic scales that show peg-and-socket articulation. ''Pteronisculus'' had enlarged [[pectoral fin]]s and small [[pelvic fin]]s. The [[dorsal fin|dorsal]] and [[anal fin]]s were virtually opposed to each other. The [[caudal fin]] was [[heterocercal]].<ref name="doi.org"/><ref name="researchgate.net"/>

''Pteronisculus'' had a wide geographic range during the Early Triassic.<ref name="sepkoskidb">{{cite journal | last = Sepkoski | first = Jack | title =  A compendium of fossil marine animal genera | journal = Bulletins of American Paleontology | volume = 364 |page=560 | year = 2002 | url = http://strata.ummp.lsa.umich.edu/jack/showgenera.php?taxon=611&rank=class | access-date = 2009-02-27 }}</ref> Fossils were collected in [[Greenland]], [[Madagascar]], [[Spitsbergen]] and the [[United States]]. It is possibly also present in the Early Triassic of [[British Columbia]], [[Canada]]; a species described as ''[[Acrolepis]] laetus'' by [[Lawrence Lambe]] has been tentatively referred to ''Pteronisculus''. From the Middle Triassic, it is only known from South [[China]].<ref name="doi.org"/><ref name="researchgate.net"/><ref name="Ren&Xu"/> Its occurrence in the [[Permian]] of [[South Africa]] has been questioned.<ref name="doi.org"/> About 13 species have been described to date, ranging from {{convert|11|cm|ft}} to {{convert|40|cm|ft}} in length.

==Classification==
''Pteronisculus'' was originally referred to the [[family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Palaeoniscidae]], but was removed due to differences to ''[[Palaeoniscum]]''.<ref name="researchgate.net">{{cite journal |last1=Xu |first1=Guang-Hui |last2=Shen |first2=Chen-Chen |last3=Zhao |first3=Li-Jun |date=2014 |title=''Pteronisculus nielseni'' sp. nov., a new stem-actinopteran fish from the Middle Triassic of Luoping, Yunnan Province, Chin |journal=Vertebrata PalAsiatica |volume=52 |pages=364–380 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268485382}}</ref> Based on similarities with the [[Late Triassic]] ''[[Turseodus]]'', it was provisionally included in [[Turseoidae]].<ref name="doi.org">{{cite journal |last1=Romano |first1=Carlo |last2=López-Arbarello |first2=Adriana |last3=Ware |first3=David |last4=Jenks |first4=James F. |last5=Brinkmann |first5=Winand |date=2019 |title=Marine Early Triassic Actinopterygii from the Candelaria Hills (Esmeralda County, Nevada, USA) |journal=Journal of Paleontology |volume=93 |issue=5 |pages=971–1000  |doi=10.1017/jpa.2019.18|bibcode=2019JPal...93..971R |s2cid=155564297 }}</ref> A [[synapomorphy]] of ''Pteronisculus'' and ''Turseodus'' is the tooth-bearing [[Lacrimal bone|lachrymal]]. However, ''Turseodus'' is incompletely known and a close relationship with ''Pteronisculus'' has not yet been tested with a [[cladistics|cladistic]] analysis. In the cladistic analysis by Ren & Xu,<ref name="Ren&Xu">{{cite journal |last1=Ren |first1=Yi |last2=Xu |first2=Guang-Hui |date=2021 |title=A new species of ''Pteronisculus'' from the Middle Triassic (Anisian) of Luoping, Yunnan, China, and phylogenetic relationships of early actinopterygian fishes |journal=Vertebrata PalAsiatica |volume=59 |pages=169–199 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353373478 |doi=10.19615/j.cnki.2096-9899.210518|s2cid=238786196 }}</ref> ''Pteronisculus'' was recovered in a [[sister group]] relationship with the [[Carboniferous]] ''[[Cyranorhis]]'', a genus that has been referred to the probably [[paraphyletic]] family [[Rhadinichthyidae]].
